The Expected (Fisher) Information

Source: R/information.R
expected_info.Rd

Selects the expected information, the Fisher information $$\mathbb{E}\left[-\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial\eta\,\partial\eta^\top} \right],$$ evaluated at the estimates. With method = NULL, the default, the closed form is used where the family writes the expected information out (see expected_hessian_exact()), and expect_opg() otherwise. An object in method is used for every family, also for one that has the closed form.

Usage

expected_info(method = NULL)

Arguments

method

NULL (the default) or an object that selects how the expectation is obtained:

  • NULL: the closed form of the family where it has one, and expect_opg() otherwise;

  • expect_opg(): the outer product of the observed scores, which costs one gradient;

  • expect_integrate(): quadrature (or summation over the support) of the observed information against the density with identity = "hessian", or of minus the outer product of the scores with identity = "score";

  • expect_mc(): Monte Carlo, with its own sample size nsim and identity.

expected_derivative_methods compares the methods. Any other value signals an error.

Value

An S7 object of class ExpectedInfo, which inherits from Information, with the property method.

See also

observed_info() for the other object; information_objects for the comparison; expected_derivative_methods for the methods; vcov.distrib_fit() for the function that takes the object.

Examples

expected_info()
#> Expected information (closed form where the family has one, otherwise the outer product of the scores)
expected_info(method = expect_mc(nsim = 2000))
#> Expected information (expectation by Monte Carlo (nsim = 2000))

set.seed(1)
d <- gamma1_distrib()
fit <- fit_distrib(d, distrib_rng(d, 300, list(mu = 3, phi = 0.6)))
vcov(fit, information = expected_info())
#>             mu         phi
#> mu  0.01710378 0.000000000
#> phi 0.00000000 0.002065084
